ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended, Articles 2 and 4-2), Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Act No. 17705), Commercial Act (Act No. 1000) as to share registers, and Real Estate Investment Trusts Act (Act No. 5373, as amended). Beneficial owner identification is further prescribed by Financial Services Commission regulations and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit customer due diligence rules under the Financial Transaction Reporting Act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified extract of the Korean commercial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path for countries party to the Apostille Convention: notarize the certified registry extract and obtain an Apostille from the competent authority in the issuer's country; for non-member states: notarize, then request Consular Legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction; one path only, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (tax clearance and no-lien certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of Korea or the corporate home-country tax authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarize, then Apostille by the competent authority; non-member state: notarize, then Consular Legalization by the Korean mission; mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation and the REIT structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the signature of the board secretary or director and affix Apostille; non-Hague path: notarize and then submit for Consular Legalization at the nearest Korean consular post; choose only one path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified Korean translation and statutory registration draft)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed abroad in an Apostille state: notarize the foreign signatures and obtain Apostille; if executed in a non-member state: notarize abroad and obtain Consular Legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate; Korean notarization for registration is a filing step, not a second authentication chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (bank due diligence and source-of-funds confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the investor or shareholder in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille member country: certifying officer signs before a notary, then Apostille; non-member country: notarize and then Consular Legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate; no mixed or sequential Apostille-then-Legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory protocols require screening all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and transaction counterparties against at least: (1) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (2) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List because USD wire rails are used; (3) Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist and domestic sanctions measures under the Act on Reporting and Using Certain Financial Transaction Information; (4) FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements; (5) Korean Financial Services Commission administrative orders; and (6) adverse media and politically exposed person indicators. For a licensed REIT, enhanced due diligence must be completed before any distribution, with confirmation documented and archived for at least five years. Prior to engaging with any Korean bank, the applicant must provide a clear organizational chart showing 25% plus direct and indirect ownership and control because the UBO register is not publicly available but is government-only-access by KoFIU and financial institutions under mandatory CDD rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Electronic Registration System; iROF)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa name must be in Korean script; the suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' or the equivalent Stock Corporation marker must appear in the statutory corporate name. Foreign names are transliterated phonetically into Hangul in accordance with the Korean Language and Alphabet Regulations; the registry index requires a distinguishable Hangul distinctive name, a business-purpose identifier, and the company-type suffix. The Romanized name in the articles must match the certified transliteration used on the corporate seal and bank account. Four-tier review is applied: (i) distinctive Hangul element; (ii) prohibited and sensitive token check; (iii) business scope and ISIC correspondence with the REIT license; and (iv) registry-identical-name and similar-name search across the same business purpose category.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant should request a written rejection notice and obtain the registry officer's stated reasons. Within one week of the disposition, an application for an appeal must be filed under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act with the district court having jurisdiction over the registry. The appeal must identify the statutory ground, the proposed name, and why it is permissible under the Commercial Act and the Real Estate Investment Trusts Act. If the registry rejects on the basis of identity or similarity with an existing name, the applicant may alternatively file a reservation for a revised name using a new distinctive Hangul element. Legal counsel should be engaged to prepare the appeal brief and, if necessary, initiate administrative litigation in the competent administrative court within 90 days of the final rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for the licensed real estate investment trust. The Real Estate Investment Trusts Act and the Korean Commercial Act require the Chusik Hoesa to maintain a physical registered office in Korea at which the board of directors, the REIT asset manager, and the statutory auditor can receive process and keep books; the National Tax Service and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport will reject a virtual address for registration, license, and value-added tax purposes. Korean banks also require the physical office to open a corporate account and to satisfy the Financial Services Commission AML CDD requirement that the registered address correspond to actual business operations. A one-person office, post-office mailbox, or service address without a lease and operational staff is insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) official Korean office lease agreement in the company name with a fixed term of at least one year; (2) visible company signage and reception; (3) board minutes and REIT committee records kept at that office; (4) on-site compliance and accounting staff or regular external service provider presence; (5) corporate seal, share register, board resolution book, and bank correspondence available for inspection; (6) utility bills, internet bill, and tax notifications addressed to the exact registered office; (7) evidence that the registered office is open during normal business hours and is not shared with more than three other unrelated business entities. Quantified risk: 85% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or the National Tax Service within the first 12 months of operation for a newly licensed REIT; 70% likelihood during the six-month period after the first dividend distribution.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, Articles 289 through 328 (formation, capital subscription, payment, directors, representative director, and registration of a Chusik Hoesa stock corporation); Commercial Registration Act, as amended; Real Estate Investment Company Act, as amended; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for non-resident investment reporting; and the Framework Act on National Taxes for post-formation business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, with electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Service (IROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Hoesa Seorip Deunggi Shincheongseo).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act: after the 2012 amendment, no minimum paid-in capital is required to incorporate a Chusik Hoesa. However, for registration as a Real Estate Investment Company under the Real Estate Investment Company Act and its Enforcement Decree, the company must satisfy the statutory paid-in capital, net asset, and equity composition requirements in force at the time of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport application. There is no statutory blocked escrow account rule under the Commercial Act, but the full subscription price must be paid into a domestic bank account and cannot be withdrawn before the Registry confirms incorporation; the bank certificate of deposit is filed with the Registry. The registration tax is 0.4 percent of declared paid-in capital plus a 20 percent education surcharge plus a fixed court fee; the 400 USD field entry is an approximate total for a KRW 100,000,000 paid-in capital case.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED BY THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK CORPORATION) ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA.

The undersigned directors, constituting the full board of the Company, hereby waive notice and hold the first meeting of the Board of Directors at the registered office. The chairperson of the meeting confirms that the certificate of incorporation has been issued by the competent District Court Registry and that the corporate existence of the Company has lawfully commenced. After deliberation, the Board unanimously resolves as follows.

1. Charter and Governance. The Articles of Incorporation of the Company are confirmed, ratified, and adopted in their entirety. The Board authorizes the representative director to adopt internal governance regulations, including rules for director meetings, contract execution, and maintenance of the corporate seal, consistent with the Commercial Act and the Real Estate Investment Company Act.

2. Share Capital Subscription. The Board confirms that the total issued shares of the Company have been lawfully subscribed and fully paid in the amount reflected in the bank certificate of deposit filed with the Registry. No share has been issued at a discount to par value. The paid-in capital account and register of shareholders shall be maintained at the registered office, and the representative director is instructed to issue share certificates to all subscribers without delay.

3. Registered Office. The registered office designated in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the legal seat of the Company. The lease and use agreement for that office is approved, and the office shall be the place of service of process, statutory books, shareholder records, and corporate administration.

4. Banking Authorization. The representative director and one additional director are jointly authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts in the name of the Company. All checks, wire instructions, payment orders, loan documents, and bank guarantees shall require the signature of the representative director together with the chief financial officer or another designated director. Banking forms and signature cards are approved as submitted.

5. Statutory Officer Appointments. [Name] is appointed President and Representative Director; [Name] is appointed Director; [Name] is appointed Statutory Auditor for the term and compensation recorded in the minutes. Each officer shall discharge duties with the standard of care required by the Commercial Act and shall cause the Company to comply with all tax, REIT licensing, anti-money laundering, and disclosure obligations.

6. Regulatory and Physical Licensing Action. The Board instructs management to obtain the business registration certificate from the National Tax Service and the Real Estate Investment Company registration from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. To the extent any physical property, construction, or workplace safety approval becomes applicable, the Board directs management to obtain all municipal building, fire safety, civil defense, and environmental permits before commencing operations.

7. Delegation. The representative director is authorized to execute all applications, contracts, bank forms, regulatory filings, and other documents necessary to give effect to these resolutions. The secretary is directed to place these resolutions in the corporate minute book and to issue certified copies as required. This written resolution is valid as if adopted at a formally convened board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, execute, and notarize the articles of incorporation (Jeonggwan).
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public registered with the Korean Notary Association in the district of the proposed registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must prepare the articles of incorporation in Korean containing the corporate name, business objects, number and par value of authorized shares, total issued share capital, paid-in capital, location of the registered office, method of public notice, share classes, and procedure for summoning the inaugural general meeting. Every promoter must execute the articles, and the notary must authenticate the signatures and confirm that the articles do not violate mandatory provisions of the Commercial Act. Foreign signatories must execute under a valid power of attorney with legalization or apostille, and all non-Korean documents must be accompanied by a certified Korean translation. The authenticated articles become the constitutive document of the Company and must be retained for submission to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Draft and final articles of incorporation in Korean
Passport or national identity documents of each promoter
Power of attorney for each foreign promoter or authorized incorporator
Apostille or consular legalization of foreign powers of attorney
Certified Korean translation of any foreign-language document
Notarial fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to defective or conflicting charter provisions, the promoters must revise the articles, re-execute the corrected version before the same notary, and pay a new notarial fee. If the defect concerns corporate purpose or capital structure, obtain legal interpretation from the Korean Bar Association or amend the charter by a new resolution before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe, pay in, and verify share capital with a domestic bank deposit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank designated by the promoters, acting as a foreign exchange bank for non-resident subscription reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each subscriber must execute a subscription application specifying the class and number of shares subscribed. The full issue price must be paid into a domestic bank account held in the name of the promoters or the company in formation before the incorporation registration is filed. For non-resident shareholders, the receiving bank must complete the foreign exchange reporting process required under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the bank must supply a certificate of deposit to evidence full payment. The promoters must prepare a capitalization table and a subscription summary sheet showing that no share is issued below par. The bank deposit certificate will be attached to the incorporation registration application and serves as the principal verification that the paid-in capital obligation has been satisfied.
required_dossiers: Share subscription applications executed by each subscriber
Subscription summary sheet with class and number of shares
Certificate of deposit or deposit receipt from the domestic bank
Foreign exchange receipt and disposition report for non-resident investors
Passports or corporate IDs of each subscriber
Bank KYC and AML declaration forms for all subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscriber fails to pay the subscribed amount, the promoters may demand performance and, if payment is still not made, rescind the subscription under the Commercial Act and re-subscribe the affected shares. If the bank reports a foreign exchange filing deficiency, submit a corrected report to the same bank; if the bank refuses the deposit certificate, select another licensed bank and re-execute the payment process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation registration with the Local District Court Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the Local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, with electronic filing via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Service (IROS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after completion of notarization and full payment of the subscription price, the representative director or authorized counsel must file the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company. The application must state the authorized capital, issued shares, names and resident numbers of directors and auditor, the representative director, the corporate seal specimen, and the registered office. The Registry will examine the notarized articles, bank deposit certificate, written consents of officers, lease evidence, and tax receipt. The applicant must pay the registration tax of 0.4 percent of declared paid-in capital, a local education surcharge equal to 20 percent of that tax, and the fixed court fee. Once approved, the Registry issues the certified corporate registration extract, and the Company comes into existence as a juridical person.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation
Notarized articles of incorporation
Bank certificate of deposit
Written consent forms of each director and the auditor
Corporate seal report and specimen of the representative director
Lease agreement or written consent for use of the registered office
Power of attorney for the filing counsel
Receipt of payment of registration tax and court fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a supplementary order, the applicant must cure the missing or defective documents within the statutory cure period. If the application is rejected, the applicant may resubmit with a corrected application and pay the fee again. A party aggrieved by a substantively unlawful rejection may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within the statutory appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the business registration certificate and complete post-formation corporate formalities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service local tax office exercising jurisdiction over the principal place of business, together with the District Court Registry for seal certificates and the reporting bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director must submit the business registration application to the relevant local tax office within the statutory filing period following establishment. The tax office will issue the business registration certificate, which assigns the corporate tax identification number and establishes the Company as a taxable person for value-added tax and corporate income tax purposes. Concurrently, the Company should obtain certified copies of the corporate seal registration and open a permanent operating bank account under the banking resolution adopted by the Board. For non-resident shareholders, the foreign direct investment report must be perfected through a foreign exchange bank. The Company must also file an initial disclosure of beneficial owners and directors for anti-money laundering compliance with respect to the real estate investment purpose.
required_dossiers: Certified extract of corporate registration from the District Court
Notarized articles of incorporation
Business registration application form
Lease agreement or ownership evidence for the registered office
Identity documents of the representative director and shareholders
Board resolution on bank account opening and authorized signatories
Foreign exchange investment report forms for non-resident investors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the real estate investment business description, submit the board resolution and REIT business plan and request a written tax ruling. If the foreign exchange report is rejected, correct the beneficiary ownership information and resubmit through the same bank. Late business registration may be cured by filing immediately and paying the applicable negligence penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Real Estate Investment Company registration from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Real Estate Investment Company Registration Section, with coordination of the Financial Services Commission for any listed or public offering REIT.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation and business registration are completed, the Company must apply for registration as a Real Estate Investment Company under the Real Estate Investment Company Act. The application must include a detailed investment and asset management policy, proof that the statutory paid-in capital and net asset conditions are satisfied, appointment of an external auditor, and either a delegation agreement with a licensed asset management company or a certification of self-management capacity. The Company must disclose the target real estate portfolio, acquisition contracts or letters of intent, projected cash flows, dividend policy, and the identity and suitability of directors and significant shareholders. For public offering REITs, the Ministry will coordinate with the Financial Services Commission on disclosure and securities regulations. Upon approval, the Ministry issues the Real Estate Investment Company registration certificate, which is the mandatory statutory license for the REIT business.
required_dossiers: Certified extract of corporate registration
Business registration certificate from the National Tax Service
Notarized articles of incorporation and board resolutions
Detailed REIT business plan and investment policy
Real estate acquisition contracts, letters of intent, or portfolio schedules
Proof of paid-in capital and bank certificates
External auditor appointment letter
Asset management agreement or self-management certification
KYC and AML questionnaires for directors, officers, and significant shareholders
Pro-forma financial statements and dividend distribution policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry issues a deficiency notice, the Company must respond within the prescribed cure period with amended documents or additional evidence. If the application is denied, the Company may resubmit after curing the specific defects or file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeals Act. If denial is caused by insufficient capital, the shareholders must pass a capital increase resolution, complete the deposit and registration amendment procedure, and then resubmit the REIT registration application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Real Estate Investment Company Registration Section, with joint coordination by the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service for public offering or listed REITs.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Real Estate Investment Company Registration Certificate (Budongsan Tujahoe-sa Deungrokjeung) under the Real Estate Investment Company Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable at formation stage for the financial and portfolio management operations of the REIT; for any future construction or development of real property, the Ministry of Environment and the relevant municipal authority under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act will become competent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable: the entity is a passive income real estate investment trust and does not operate ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx, or 52xx physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facilities. No environmental impact assessment registration is required for the corporate formation. If the REIT later launches a construction or development project, the classification will be determined under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act at project level.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable at the incorporation stage. If future physical development occurs, the REIT must comply with project-level wastewater discharge thresholds under the Water Environment Conservation Act, volatile organic compound and air emission limits under the Clean Air Conservation Act, and hazardous waste handling standards under the Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable at the corporate formation stage. The REIT is a financial vehicle holding real estate assets for income; no civil defense fire permit is issued to the entity itself. At asset level, any occupied or operated building must be covered by the building occupancy certificate under the Building Act, fire safety installation standards under the Fire Services Act, and workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. These certificates are inspected and enforced by the local municipal government and the National Fire Agency as applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the electronic tax administration portal HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Customs and export clearance functions relevant to export zero-rating are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) via the UNI-PASS electronic system. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) issues the statutory license or approval required for a Real Estate Investment Trust under the Real Estate Investment Company Act before the NTS business registration becomes fully effective.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act through court registration at the local registry office and obtain the corporate registration certificate. If foreign capital is involved, complete the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA to obtain the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. Step 2: After MOLIT REIT approval or license issuance, the statutory representative or an appointed tax agent files a Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business within 20 days from business commencement, in accordance with Article 5-4 of the Value Added Tax Act and Article 51 of the Corporate Income Tax Act. Step 3: The NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit business registration number that functions as the single national tax identification number, the VAT registration number, and the e-invoice identifier for the entity. Step 4: A foreign entity that does not yet have a domestic place of business must appoint a domestic tax representative in accordance with Article 82 of the Framework Act on National Taxes to apply for a TIN or temporary VAT refund registration. Step 5: The REIT must also complete VAT payer registration as a general taxpayer; the simplified taxpayer regime is not available to corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (default): a resident Chusik Hoesa is treated as a separate taxable person subject to corporate income tax on its worldwide income, with a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax; there is no group or consolidated filing regime. Pass_Through_Eligible (REIT special): a qualifying listed REIT may deduct dividends actually paid out of the current fiscal year distributable income under Article 51-2 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, effectively achieving a pass-through tax result for distributed rental income and capital gains, subject to continued listing and payment of at least 90% of distributable income. Territorial_Scope: not the default for a domestic corporation, because resident entities are taxed on worldwide income. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box classification election exists in Korea; tax classification follows the legal form under the Commercial Act. Election 1 (REIT dividend deduction): a listed REIT may elect to deduct dividends distributed within the statutory period, provided it distributes at least 90% of distributable income and satisfies the listing, debt-to-equity, and asset composition requirements under Article 51-2 of the Corporate Income Tax Act. Election 2 (special tax reductions on acquisitions): the REIT may elect to claim a 50% reduction of acquisition tax and registration tax on qualifying real estate acquisitions made under the statutory REIT management period and resale restrictions. Election 3 (deferral of capital gains on contributed assets): an electing REIT may defer corporate tax on gains realized when shareholders contribute real estate in exchange for REIT shares under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, subject to holding-period conditions. Election 4 (international tax elections): Korea applies hybrid mismatch adjustment rules under Article 27 of the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs, which disallow deductions in Korea where the same payment is deductible in the counterparty jurisdiction; this operates as a conformity rule rather than a discretionary taxpayer election, and requires annual documentation of cross-border hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act, administered by the NTS on a quarterly filing basis. The system is supplemented by a Local Consumption Tax equal to 10% of the national VAT remitted to local governments, and by customs duties and individual consumption taxes applicable to certain luxury real estate and specific goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory economic turnover threshold exists for a Chusik Hoesa or a REIT; every business operator must register with the competent district tax office within 20 days of business commencement regardless of revenue. The simplified taxpayer threshold of KRW 80,000,000 of annual turnover is available only to individuals and is unavailable to corporations. The REIT must therefore always maintain general taxpayer status, issue VAT tax invoices, and file quarterly VAT returns even when all rental income is derived from residential leases subject to transitional taxation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is mandatory for all B2B supplies and all taxpayers since July 1, 2022, pursuant to Article 32 of the Value Added Tax Act. Every e-invoice must be transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system through the HomeTax portal itself, the HomeTax Open Application Programming Interface (API), or a certified e-invoice service provider, no later than the day following the supply date. Korea does not operate a Latin American style pre-clearance fiscal stamping regime; instead, the NTS performs near real-time reconciliation of e-invoices, cash receipts, and quarterly VAT returns, assigning a unique acceptance reference number to each e-invoice. For B2C receipts, business operators must issue cash receipts for cash payments over KRW 100,000, which applies to rental collections from individual tenants. The REIT must transmit monthly rental e-invoices and register new tenant supplies in the HomeTax system before the statutory issue deadline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies to goods exported from the Korean customs territory upon filing and clearance of an export declaration with the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS. Services: zero-rating applies to (i) services supplied to a non-resident or a foreign corporation where the place of supply and place of actual use are outside Korea, (ii) international transportation services, and (iii) foreign-currency-earning service categories prescribed by Presidential Decree, provided payment is collected in foreign currency or in Korean currency with an approved bank record. For the Korean REIT, rental and disposal of real estate located in Korea remains subject to 10% VAT even if the counter-party is a foreign resident; however, real estate located outside Korea is outside the scope of Korean VAT, and asset-management or advisory services rendered to a foreign fund or foreign asset owner qualify as zero-rated supplies where the place of use is overseas and the consideration is received from abroad. The zero-rated export or offshore supply must be substantiated by evidence retained for at least five years from the date of supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) issued through the KCS UNI-PASS system with the electronic export report number
Commercial invoice and itemized packing list matched to the export declaration
Transport documents: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), cargo manifest, or courier delivery receipt evidencing departure to the overseas destination

Foreign exchange evidence: Certificate of Purchase of Foreign Exchange or the bank foreign exchange transaction record showing collection of the export proceeds within the statutory 18-month collection period
Sales contract or purchase order together with, for service exports, a service performance report, statement of the place of supply, and the foreign counterparty identification records
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice containing the zero-rate code and the export reference remarks
REIT-specific transaction documentation: asset management agreements, custodian records, foreign fund subscription documents, and repatriation instructions for cross-border property transactions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS audits export zero-rating and refund claims by systematically cross-matching the KCS export declaration database, bank foreign exchange records, and HomeTax e-invoice data. If export proceeds are not collected within the statutory 18-month collection period, or within an approved extension granted by the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, the zero-rating is retroactively revoked and the supply is reclassified as taxable at 10% VAT, with the tax collected together with overdue interest at the statutory national tax interest rate of 3.5% per annum and general negligent nonpayment penalties. Where documentation is false or fabricated, the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes understatement penalties of 20% or 40% of the underpaid VAT depending on the degree of intention, in addition to negligent reporting penalties; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment for up to two years or a fine of up to three times the tax evaded, increased to five years and a fivefold fine for habitual offenders. The Korea Customs Service may also impose customs fines for false export declarations and suspend or revoke the exporter registration. Bank guarantees, refund freezing, and personal joint and several liability of the REIT directors and its tax representative may be ordered under Article 38 of the Framework Act on National Taxes where fraudulent refunds or zero-rating claims are detected.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, with Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) policy oversight, delegated FX-bank execution, and reporting through the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The Korea Customs Service enforces border-side collection and suspicious cross-border trade settlement controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 3: current transactions including trade settlements, services, interest, dividends, royalties, and normal short-term banking credits are freely convertible without prior exchange-control approval, provided the remittance is executed through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank and reported to the Bank of Korea through FEIS. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment into the REIT, acquisition of Korean real estate or securities by non-residents, cross-border loans, guarantees, and return-of-capital distributions, are subject to prior reporting, approval, or registration requirements. Profit remittance hurdles for a Chusik Hoesa REIT are manageable: dividends from the REIT qualify as investment income in the current account only where the foreign investor is a registered shareholder, the distribution is validly declared out of distributable profits, corporate income tax is settled, and withholding tax at the domestic 22 percent rate or treaty-reduced rate is documented. The remitting bank will require the shareholder register extract, dividend resolution, tax number, beneficial-ownership statement, and the applicable FEIS purpose code. There is no fixed KRW convertibility quota, but banks apply single-transaction thresholds, BOP statistical coding, and anti-money-laundering suspicious-transaction screening; a large or structured remittance may be held pending internal compliance clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The REIT is not an exporter and has no statutory export-proceeds collection burden. For any trading or group companies operating an export book, Korea no longer imposes a mandatory conversion ratio or a surrender-to-central-bank obligation; resident exporters may retain export earnings in foreign-currency deposit accounts. The statutory collection timeline is that export proceeds must be received within 18 months from the date of the export declaration under Article 6-7 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. BOK and MOEF may grant an extension for justified commercial disputes, insolvency, or receivable restructuring. Failure to collect within the deadline must be reported through the relevant foreign exchange bank and may trigger administrative fines. In practice, foreign-currency receipts should be repatriated to a domestic foreign-currency account promptly and disclosed in the periodic foreign exchange transaction report; conversion into KRW is made through the bank's market rate and is an eligible current-account conversion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and audit report submission under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service via the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 for listed entities and KRW 20,000,000 for non-listed entities; persistent non-submission may trigger a regulatory demand and referral to enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual real estate investment company operation report and compliance statement under the Real Estate Investment Company Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end, or the date prescribed in the REIT registration approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning, imposition of corrective orders, and possible revocation of REIT registration in cases of repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local income tax surcharge return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service and the competent local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; consolidated and group filers may apply the extended four-month deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20 percent of the understated tax plus monthly delinquency interest of 0.022 percent; continuous failure may lead to seizure of assets and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and shareholder ownership confirmation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors; retained for inspection by the Financial Supervisory Service, National Tax Service, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual ordinary general shareholders meeting, covering all share transfers during the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors subject to non-penalty fines under the Commercial Act; failure to maintain accurate statutory registers may void the evidential effect of the registers and trigger administrative penalty actions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all licensed REIT entities under the Real Estate Investment Company Act; additionally for a general Chusik Hoesa if total assets at fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion, annual revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion, or the company is listed or licensed as a financial company
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to REITs and audit-mandated stock corporations; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) may apply only to small non-audited corporations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each ordinary general shareholders meeting, the directors must verify that the register of members accurately reflects all share transfers, pledges, and beneficial ownership changes from the preceding fiscal year; the confirmation is minuted and retained with supporting transfer documentation. Any change crossing statutory notification thresholds must be reported to the Korea Securities Depository or Financial Supervisory Service under capital market rules and disclosed in the annual business report.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and preferential deductions available under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law, including the Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax reductions for qualifying FDI, the REITs Special Act tax exemptions on qualifying distribution income, small and medium enterprise tax rates (9%-19%), and the progressive corporate tax rates: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% for income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion, 21% for income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion, and 24% for income exceeding KRW 300 billion (subject to the 25% headline rate including local income tax surcharges).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing system; Form 1065 (Corporate Tax Return) and accompanying schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for calendar-year entities), with a 1-month automatic extension available upon application; quarterly prepayment obligations for corporations with annual tax liability exceeding KRW 10 million

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number and corporate identification details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Korean business registration number assigned at incorporation; foreign entities must register with the NTS through their domestic place of effective management or permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the fiscal year, calculated as gross revenue minus allowable deductions and prior-year loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute in KRW on a calendar-year basis unless a different fiscal year is approved by the NTS; attach a reconciliation statement reconciling book income to taxable income under the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax amount computed at progressive rates, plus additional taxes (surtaxes) for qualifying entities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive rate schedule applicable to domestic corporations; foreign corporations are taxed only on Korea-source income at the same rates unless a tax treaty provides otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax (Surtax) on corporate tax liability, typically 10% of the corporate tax amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the local income tax surtax as a separate return (Form 1065-1) or within the combined return depending on the local government portal; non-residents must pay via a designated domestic financial institution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit claim for taxes paid in a source country against Korean corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 1065-8 (Foreign Tax Credit) and provide evidence of foreign tax payment, including certified tax payment receipts and tax assessment documents; treaty relief does not preclude the foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total prepaid taxes, withholding taxes, and interim self-assessed payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report quarterly prepayments and any Korean withholding taxes on interest, dividends, royalties, or other Korea-source payments; claim refund support by attaching withholding certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable amount after credits and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the net balance through the National Tax Collection Account; electronic filing and payment are mandatory for entities with gross revenue exceeding KRW 100 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related party transaction disclosure (Transfer Pricing Summary Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify all cross-border transactions with related parties in the special category box; attaching a Local File is mandatory where the threshold criteria are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax for the first month and 1% per additional month, capped at 20% (or 25% if non-payment is intentional); unfaithful and negligent return penalties of 5%; valuation and calculation error penalty of 5%; daily surcharge of 0.025% (9.125% annualized) for underpayment or outstanding balances after the due date; additional penalties for the failure to issue tax invoices or file payment statements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (including 10% local income tax surcharge on the 22% corporate income tax rate, but for dividend withholding under the Corporate Tax Act and Income Tax Act, the rate is 22% plus 2.2% local income tax surcharge, effectively 24.2%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke tax treaty relief, the beneficial owner must file Form 1107 (Application for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction) with the paying Korean withholding agent before or at the time of payment; a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) must be issued by the foreign tax authority, translated into Korean or English, and notarized or apostilled as applicable under the Hague Apostille Convention; the NTS may request additional beneficial ownership documentation (including a statement of business purpose, organizational chart, and financial substance) and may deny relief for conduit situations within a 2-year statute of limitations; routine administrative review and appeal rights apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalty withholding tax: statutory rate 22% plus 2.2% local income tax surcharge (24.2% total); treaty rates typically reduce to 15% or 10% depending on intellectual property type (e.g., under the Korea-US DTA 10% for industrial royalties, 15% for copyright royalties) with domestic minimum interest rates applied to deemed royalties; interest withholding tax: statutory rate 22% plus 2.2% local income tax surcharge (24.2% total); treaty rate often 10%-15% for arm's length non-bank interest, and exemption or 0% for state institutions and qualified central banks; all treaty reductions require a TRC and beneficial ownership declaration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 million per related-party cross-border transaction for Local File/Master File requirements; KRW 50 million for intercompany services and technology transfers; KRW 100 million for intercompany financing transactions; country-by-country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue at or above KRW 100 billion for the preceding fiscal year.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Yes, the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) doctrine applies in the context of the Korean modified ESR concept under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA); while Korea is not a zero-tax jurisdiction and does not impose the UAE-style ESR regime, Korean tax law requires economic substance for tax treaty benefits as a core element of the beneficial ownership analysis and general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) adopted under the OECD BEPS initiative; a Korean chusik hoesa (REIT or ordinary corporation) must demonstrate real business purpose, local employees, office, and decision-making to avoid treaty shopping and substance-based penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of taxable income, false bookkeeping, destruction of accounting records, use of fabricated invoices, or deliberate underpayment exceeding KRW 50 million within 3 years; or transactions designed to hide cross-border related-party profits without arm's length substantiation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 10 years for fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act if the amount evaded exceeds KRW 100 million), or a fine up to KRW 150 million; additional cartel surcharges increase tax up to 40%; criminal investigation referral by the NTS with public disclosure on the NTS website.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, representatives, and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for underpaid corporate tax, penalties, and unpaid payroll withholdings; civil restitution of evaded amounts, personal travel bans, departure restrictions, seizure of personal assets, and, upon conviction, imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 10 years for aggravated evasion).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a paper corporation with no real office, employees, business decisions, or revenue-generating activity; using the Korean entity solely to park funds, issue invoices, or decorate a corporate veil; failing to meet the REIT statutory asset distribution requirements or asset management substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of preferential REIT taxation (including distribution deduction), full retroactive corporate income tax recapture, denial of treaty benefits, administrative fine up to 200% of the tax benefit, business registration cancellation, and mandatory delisting from the Korea Exchange; the NCIS-PRIS or KFTC may also impose financial sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally responsible for the entity's liabilities under the Court-ordered clause if corporate formalities are ignored; the national tax collection law imposes joint liability on directors for taxes payable and penalties; criminal prosecution for violation of the REITs Act or Fraud Act and civil damages; travel bans and asset freezes in aggravated shell corporate conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to apply customer due diligence when receiving rent payments, dividends, or proceeds from real estate disposals; handling proceeds from illegal sources through the REIT bank accounts; structuring transactions (smurfing) below the threshold to avoid reporting; or failing to report suspicious transactions above KRW 20 million (or equivalent foreign currency) to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment of 3 to 5 years; fines up to KRW 100 million; administrative penalty 20% of the value of the transaction; suspension of the entity's operational license under the Real Estate Investment Company Act; KoFIU can impose corrective action and hold management accountable; confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate or conceal AML breaches are personally liable and may be imprisoned; the court can impose criminal fines and disgorgement of profits; travel restrictions during an investigation, asset seizure, and prohibition from holding licensed positions such as asset manager, compliance officer or representative director under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a foreign shareholder without withholding tax and remitting the net amount directly abroad, failing to secure a TRC when invoking a treaty, misclassifying loans as equity to avoid interest withholding, or using a back-to-back loan arrangement lacking arm's length terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax on gross payment recaptured at the 24.2% statutory rate, plus 25% deficiency penalty, plus a daily surcharge of 0.025%; a penalty for omission of withholding equal to 5% of the delinquent amount; additional penalties for negligence; treaty benefits can be denied and the foreign payee placed on the NTS non-compliance list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors and financial officers who signed remittance instructions are personally liable for unwithheld amounts and penalties as withholding agents; civil restitution for cross-border loss of tax revenue; travel bans, criminal prosecution for a failure to withhold and remit under the tax code; if the offshore benefit is hidden in personal accounts, personal asset forfeiture follows.
